title: Usability, Econ, and SLA Roadmap Brainstorm

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-09-01 15:00 PDT, Duration: ~52m, Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Jonas (Arcadia Head of ML), Priyanka (Arcadia CTO), Ella (Arcadia Platform), Samir (Arcadia FinOps).

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick round of intros — we'll keep this a brain dump / roadmap alignment, not a formal deck presentation.
[00:18] Jonas: Sounds good. We've got a tight cost window heading into Q4 so we want to see where we can shave per-request cost without breaking checkout latency.
[00:26] Samir: Yeah finance is, uh, leaning on us to lower the monthly burn by 18% by end of year, so any hard numbers will help.
[00:35] Liam: Totally. High level: there are three levers we usually recommend — batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization/model size trade. We can run a combined strategy and show modeled savings plus measured latency deltas.
[00:48] Priyanka: For checkout, our p95 needs to be under 250ms, global. We have some regional spikes in EU.
[00:56] Lily (mislabelled speaker, likely Maya): Understood. Quick clarifying q — is that 250ms end-to-end including network, or just inference?
[01:05] Ella: End-to-end, browser to response. We measure from edge LB to client render.
[01:10] Liam: Okay that changes the headroom. If we look at inference-only targets, we can be in 70–120ms p95 with a small model and aggressive batching. But network and app latencies eat the rest.
[01:25] Jonas: Can you quantify "aggressive" batching? For checkout we can't add 400ms.
[01:31] Liam: Yeah, aggressive batching is a continuous batch size that sometimes waits a few ms to form bigger micro-batches. For user-facing checkout we recommend micro-batches capped at 8–12 tokens or a 10ms max wait. That usually keeps perceived latency low while improving GPU efficiency.
[01:47] Samir: And cost — what kind of %-age reduction are we talking?
[01:51] Liam: Batching + prefix caching often hits 20–40% token cost reduction depending on repeat prompts. Quantization (int8/4-bit) can cut model throughput cost another 15–35% but may slightly change generation quality in edge cases.
[02:11] Priyanka: We run some reranking and long-context product description generations; those aren't as latency-sensitive. Could we route those to a cheaper quantized model?
[02:19] Maya: Yes, smart routing is exactly the pattern we push — latency-sensitive endpoints to a low-latency variant, background jobs to cheaper quantized variants. We can show a routing POC.
[02:29] Jonas: About private deployment — our security team prefers a VPC private control plane. Is that full private or hybrid?
[02:36] Priya: Also need to know about KMS integration and audit logs — procurement is going to ask.
[02:41] Priya R. (Redwood CSM misattributed): Short answer: Redwood Private can be VPC-hosted with customer KMS and full audit logs. We'll send SOC2 artifacts and an SSO + SAML integration guide.
[02:54] Ella: Are there any hidden infra costs for the VPC? Like egress or sustained GPU pricing we need to plan for?
[02:59] Maya: For Private we show a line item for managed control plane + compute. Dedicated pools (reserved) give predictable throughput and reduce per-token variability. We can model both hosted and dedicated reserve pricing for you.
[03:12] Samir: Please do — finance wants three scenarios.
[03:16] Liam: We'll put together a perf workshop plan. Ideally we run a 24-hour throughput spike test to see auto-scale behavior. We'll also validate KV cache warmup and suffix/prefix cache hit rates.
[03:29] Jonas: How intrusive are the tests? We can't disrupt production checkout flows.
[03:33] Liam: We do staged tests — start with synthetic traffic in a canary VPC or staging environment that mirrors your traffic, then a controlled small percent of real traffic if you're comfortable. We'll collaborate on throttles and rollback.
[03:46] Priyanka: On the SOC2 docs — procurement needs a SOC2 type II summary and specifics about PBKDF2/managed KMS? Also SSO for admin console.
[03:55] Maya: We'll send the SOC2 summary, the KMS integration doc (KMS/HSM options), and the SSO/SAML admin setup guide.
[04:03] Ella: Quick aside — we observed a pattern where KV caching wasn't winning because our request signatures were slightly different each time due to a timestamp field. Any suggestions?
[04:12] Liam: Normalize the prompt signatures server-side — strip ephemeral IDs or move them to structured metadata so the KV key stays stable. We can share a short snippet for your platform.
[04:24] Jonas: Nice. Also question on rollouts: if we pin model versions for a canary, how does Redwood handle fallback if the canary fails?
[04:32] Priya R.: We support automatic fallback policies by route and model family; you can configure percentage rollouts and automatic rollback thresholds based on error rate or latency.
[04:44] Samir: Returning to costs — can you show a spreadsheet with token-level math and a forecast if we move 30% of background jobs to quantized variants?
[04:52] Maya: Yep, that's part of the three scenarios. We'll include forecast assumptions and a sensitivity table (cache hit rates, batch size, qps).
[05:00] Jonas: Any competitors we should watch — we've had internal folks ping OpenAI and Anthropic for a hosted evaluation.
[05:07] Maya: Common. We can run a relative perf/cost snapshot if helpful but our focus will be on production economics and guardrails.
[05:15] Priya: One more technical — do you support tokenizer parity? We use a custom tokenizer in some models and don't want drift when routing to Redwood-hosted models.
[05:24] Liam: We can preserve tokenization by shipping your tokenizer as part of the model package or run a compatibility shim. There's often a small perf tradeoff but it's manageable.
[05:36] Jonas: Alright, let's talk timeline — Samir is pushing for decisions by mid-October. What's a realistic pilot start?
[05:42] Maya: If you share sample traffic and enable a staging VPC by early September, we can kick a performance workshop the week of Sep 8, run benching through mid-September, and start a small private pilot in October. That aligns with your mid-Oct decision.
[05:58] Samir: Good. We'll try to get the sample trace to you by Friday.
[06:03] Ella: Action: I'll upload the baseline token breakdown and a small 48-hour trace.
[06:09] Maya: Great. We'll capture next steps in the notes and send a consolidated follow-up.
[06:14] (brief overlap chatter)
[06:20] Maya: Recap — Redwood sends three pricing scenarios and SOC2/SSO docs, Liam sends perf workshop plan, Arcadia shares traces and targets, group schedules 2-hour workshop. Any objections?
[06:32] Priyanka: No objections. Just, uh, please be explicit about any data residency constraints for the private pilot.
[06:38] Maya: Noted — we'll include region-level residency notes.
[06:42] Jonas: Cool. Thanks everyone.
[06:45] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the workshop and the docs.

End transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: several speaker labels autoassigned (Lily instead of Maya in one spot), occasional punctuation missing. A few technical terms may be mistranscribed ("KV cache" as "K V cash" in raw notes).

References shared during call: "Arcadia token breakdown.csv" (uploaded post-call), "Redwood SOC2-summary.pdf" (to be sent), "Perf workshop checklist (draft)" (to be shared by Liam).
